title: Implement stronger fork choice rules
description:
Document LongestChain fork choice limitation (Layer 3 of fix)

Current Status: Using sc_consensus::LongestChain fork choice strategy

Problem: LongestChain prioritizes longer chains over chains with proper PPFA authorization. This means a longer unauthorized chain can override a shorter valid chain.

Immediate Action: For now, keep LongestChain as duplicate block rejection (Layer 2) will prevent forks from propagating. The duplicate check happens BEFORE fork choice, so conflicting blocks are rejected.

Future Enhancement: Implement PPFAAwareForkChoice that:
1. Tracks PPFA authorization status per block
2. Prioritizes chains with valid PPFA seals
3. Rejects chains with unauthorized proposers

Why Keep LongestChain Now: With Layer 2 (duplicate block rejection), forks are prevented at import time, so fork choice strategy is less critical. The duplicate rejection ensures only one block per height is accepted.

Testing: Verify that duplicate block rejection (Layer 2) works correctly before considering fork choice changes.

title: Investigate and fix consensus forking issue causing nodes to be on different blocks
description:
Investigate and fix consensus forking - Root cause identified, solution ready

STATUS: Root cause identified and complete fix designed. Ready for implementation.

ROOT CAUSE (CONFIRMED):
- Slot numbers calculated from local SystemTime::now() → clock drift
- Multiple validators think they're authorized for same slot
- No runtime API verification before block production
- No duplicate block rejection mechanism
- LongestChain fork choice accepts unauthorized chains

SOLUTION: 4-Layer defense system (see etrid-k60 for details)

IMPLEMENTATION TASKS:
1. etrid-m4w (P1) - Add duplicate block rejection (Layer 2) - SAFEST FIRST
2. etrid-bxk (P1) - Document fork choice limitation (Layer 3)
3. etrid-xf0 (P1) - Add runtime API check before production (Layer 1.2) - IN PROGRESS
4. etrid-y3q (P2) - Calculate slots from chain state (Layer 1.1)

COMPLETED:
- etrid-puf - PPFA seal validation already working (lines 633-687)

NEXT STEPS:
1. Implement Layer 2 first (etrid-m4w) - minimal risk
2. Test in devnet to verify duplicate rejection works
3. Implement Layer 1 (etrid-xf0, etrid-y3q)
4. Deploy to mainnet with coordinated validator restart

CLOSE THIS ISSUE when: All 4 layers implemented and tested successfully.

title: Fix consensus forking issue: Multiple validators producing blocks for same slot
description:
FIX IN PROGRESS: Primary fix implemented in asf_service.rs with runtime API verification before block production. Working on additional fixes to strengthen the system.

Nodes are forking because multiple validators are producing blocks for the same slot/PPFA index. The PPFA rotation and slot timing mechanism needs to be synchronized across all nodes to prevent multiple validators from believing they are authorized for the same slot. This causes chain forks when different nodes accept different blocks for the same block number.

Root cause analysis:
1. In asf_service.rs, the PPFA proposer loop runs independently on each node
2. Slot timing may drift between nodes causing different validators to believe they're authorized for the same slot
3. The committee rotation state might not be perfectly synchronized across all nodes
4. Network delays can cause timing discrepancies in slot calculations

Specific issue:
- BASE_SLOT_DURATION is 6000ms (6 seconds) but slot timing is calculated independently per node
- Genesis time may differ between nodes causing slot number calculation differences
- No mechanism to ensure only one validator produces a block per logical slot

Fixed:
1. Added runtime API verification in block production loop (etrid-xf0) - DONE

Remaining fixes needed:
2. Strengthen block import validation for PPFA authorization
3. Enhance the PPFA rotation algorithm to be more deterministic across nodes
4. Add block validation that rejects blocks from unauthorized proposers for the current slot
5. Implement a consensus-based slot number calculation that all nodes agree on

title: Strengthen block import validation for PPFA authorization
description:
Add duplicate block rejection in AsfVerifier (Layer 2.1 of fix)

Implementation Location: asf_service.rs ~line 560 (in AsfVerifier verify method, AFTER header extraction)

Purpose: Prevents forks by rejecting blocks that conflict with already-accepted blocks at same block number. This implements a First-Seen rule at the import level.

Key Change: Check if block at this height already exists with different hash - if so, reject the new block.

Why This Works: Once a block is accepted for block #N, any subsequent block for #N with different hash is rejected, forcing all nodes to commit to the same chain.

Testing: Test with multiple validators attempting to produce blocks for same slot - only first should be accepted.

title: Improve slot timer synchronization
description:
Calculate slot numbers from finalized block timestamps (Layer 1.1 of fix)

Implementation Location: asf_service.rs ~line 1474 (replace SystemTime::now() usage)

Current Problem: Slot numbers calculated from local SystemTime::now(), causing clock drift between nodes. Different validators may calculate different slot numbers, leading to multiple blocks for same logical slot.

Solution: Use chain state (finalized block timestamps) instead of local time.

Key Changes:
1. Get best block header from chain
2. Calculate expected slot from block number and slot duration
3. Calculate current slot from genesis time and current timestamp
4. Ensure slots align (within tolerance of 1)
5. Only proceed if slots match

Benefits:
- All nodes calculate slots from same chain state
- Clock drift between nodes is irrelevant
- Deterministic slot calculation across all validators

Dependencies: None (can be implemented independently)

Testing: Test with multiple validators with intentionally skewed clocks - all should calculate same slot numbers.
